## RCA / close — defect-origin attribution

**Mechanism (already proven + fixed by merged change 2362, commit `4d1567206fb4`, `rebar-ticket: e1d9-4c8e-3fd1-41c2`, LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1, MERGED):**
`/health` (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, `register_health_route`) returned a bare 200 that never
exercised the MCP request path, and `autodeploy.sh`'s blue-green `mcp` target promoted the nginx
`/mcp/` upstream on that bare 200 (`curl -fsS .../health` → flip) without ever issuing one `/mcp`
request. A container whose allowlist admitted the wrong host answered 200 while 421-ing real
traffic, and was still promoted (measured on the box 2026-08-28: promoted 54 s before serving its
first request). The fix drives one real `initialize` through the server's own
`StreamableHTTPSessionManager` inside the ASGI lifespan and publishes a `handshake` object on
`/health`; the cutover now refuses to flip when `handshake.ok` is present and false.

**Defect origin: `6964-40bb-46c9-48a7`** (story "Extend autodeploy (ADR 0079) to an mcp target
with its own in-flight drain gate"; introducing commit `2a0a4b19f2ab` "infra: add mcp blue-green
autodeploy target", `rebar-ticket: 6964-40bb-46c9-48a7`, 2026-08-25).
Class: **`plan_defect`** — a scope-of-work omission in the cutover story's plan.

**Why this ticket, not the `/health` endpoint's origin (`fd4a-4e91-f179-4932`, commit
`8297083532a3`, 2026-08-25 01:13):**
- The obligation violated is *"prove a container can serve an MCP request before flipping
  production traffic to it."* That obligation is **created by the act of promoting**, i.e. by the
  blue-green cutover gate — introduced in `2a0a4b19f2ab` (story `6964`), whose plan (steps 4–5:
  "Health-check the NEW `/health` 200 … Atomically flip the nginx `/mcp/` upstream") defines
  readiness as a bare 200 and never requires exercising `/mcp`.
- **Date test.** The "promotes a container that has never served one" behavior only became
  possible when the promote-on-200 cutover shipped (`2a0a4b19f2ab`, 2026-08-25 09:14). Before it,
  nothing auto-promoted on `/health`, so nothing was wrong. `fd4a`'s `/health` route
  (`8297083532a3`, 08:13 earlier the same day) predates the promotion consumer and was
  correct-at-the-time for its designed purpose (docker HEALTHCHECK liveness + the certified-op
  in-flight drain gauge). Blaming it would be the classic "consumer's old, correct-at-the-time
  site" mis-attribution — it is a **carrier**, not the origin.
- **Reviewer plausibility.** A reviewer of story `6964`'s blue-green cutover plan could plausibly
  have caught it: a `/health` 200 (a route deliberately OUTSIDE the auth + DNS-rebinding transport
  guard) does not prove the container can serve a real `/mcp` request, yet the plan flips
  production traffic on exactly that signal. The missing request-path proof falls squarely under
  that story's scope.

`caused_by = 6964-40bb-46c9-48a7` is recorded on the close via the ungated `--caused-by` flag
(not a forced `rebar link`; no `--force` used on any surface).

**Acceptance criteria reconciliation:** all 14 ACs are code/CI-verifiable (named unit/facade/
script tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, affected-tests-pass, and per-edit revert-required-
to-fail) and are satisfied by the landed change 2362 (all 10 named tests present in the tree;
`tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py` = 19 passed locally; CI Verified +1 covers lint/
typecheck/tests). **None require a live deploy, operator action, or shared-system verification**,
so this bug is NOT operator-gated — the "on the box" figures are motivating evidence, not ACs.
All AC checkboxes ticked.

Closing `in_progress → closed`, `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=6964-40bb-46c9-48a7`.
